text.text_excerpt: Dolly's has the best non-standard roast beef po-boy I've ever had. So what do I mean when I say non-standard? Am I some sort of roast beef snob? If you keep reading, I'll tell you. For me, a roast beef po-boy should have homemade roast beef, gravy and Leidenheimer type French Bread. Many small grocery stores and delis use a much softer loaf of bread and use boring sliced roast beef and canned gravy. Well I am here to tell you ladies and gentlemen that Dolly's version is pretty damn good. Sure it uses plain ole sliced roast beef and thin gravy, but for some reason it works. It's by far the best gas station sandwich I've ever had. That's right, this is also a gas station. In fact, the whole...

Every time I'm in the neighborhood I stop off at Dolly's for breakfast(all day). It's a no-food-filler good ole traditional breakfast. The 3-egg platter with smoke sausage, grits/hasbrowns, toast is just $10. If you're looking for lunch they have burgers and po-boys. The shrimp are a nice size, no miniatures. Their is no combo with a drink that I could see so you grab a drink from the coolers(colas to beer). #FirstWorldProblems

Dolly's looks shady as all get out. I was a little nervous walking in here thinking I was going to shanked, or even worse, my poboy wasn't going to be good. Thankfully neither of those things happened so I'm passing along my recommendation to you fine people. I waked in a ordered a shrimp poboy on a bun. I had a seat in the dining room and the cook called my up when it was ready. The shrimp were great and there were plenty of them. No complaints there. The tv was on Fox News and it was wayyyy too loud and that was pretty annoying, however. When you're done eating you take your ticket up to the cashier and pay.
